newsitem.title: FINLAND: FOCUS - Outokumpu blames markets for slump.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - Outokumpu blames markets for slump.

text.p: Finnish mining and metals group Outokumpu Oy on Monday blamed weak metal markets for a 92 percent slump in its January-August profit, warning again that full-year earnings will be considerably weaker than 1995.

Reporting profit before extraordinary items and tax slid to 109 million markka ($23.9 million) from 1.32 billion in the year-ago period, Outokumpu said copper, ferrochrome and stainless steel prices fell the sharpest.
"The result for the financial year 1996 will be considerably weaker than in 1995," Outokumpu warned in a statement.
"Although the group's financial performance is expected to improve to some extent in late 1996, the result of the last tertial will also be poor."
In 1995, the group reported a 1.48 billion markka profit before extraordinaries and tax on net sales of 16.95 billion.

January-August net sales fell only slightly to 11.08 billion markka from 11.15 billion, but the company's operating profit collapsed to 331 million from 1.36 billion and earnings per share to 0.28 markka from 7.54.
Outokumpu issued a profits warning on September 2, and although Monday's figures were at the low end of forecasts its shares responded calmly, falling 0.30 markka to 80.70 in thin midday trade.

Describing a 304 million markka operating loss at its base metals division over the period as "weaker than expected", Outokumpu blamed low metal prices and inventory losses, plus special charges in the second four months of the year.
It said the division would remain loss-making in 1996.
Outokumpu chief executive Jyrki Juusela said the company expected the price of copper to remain unchanged in the near future but zinc to rise gradually over the next few years.
"The copper price is low at the moment. We have no reason to expect any significant improvement, the copper price could rather stay at this level," he told a news conference.
"In zinc, we expect a clear improvement in the long term, in the next few years," he said. "Nickel is the most difficult to predict. We expect it to rise somewhat."
Very low copper inventories were likely to rise again towards the end of 1996, Outokumpu said.
"Copper was the only Outokumpu-produced base that showed some growth in consumption from 1995, whereas the consumption of nickel and zinc declined," it said in the statement.

"Copper inventories are at a very low level at the moment, but increasing supply toward year-end is predicted to result in growth in inventories. Nickel and zinc inventories are still higher than normal."

In stainless steel, where the average German transaction price fell 16 percent from the first four months of the year to the second, Outokumpu said "market conditions have remained unchanged except for a slight decline in prices."
The outlook for stainless steel markets remain clouded by uncertainty, but demand is expected to grow and prices to rise somewhat by the end of the year.
The company sees Europe's overall economic growth speeding up in late 1996, and demand for metals and metal products strengthening as a result. ($ = 4.564 Finnish Markka)
